items.entity: 2-D cantilever design domain (length L x height H)
items.description: Sec. II.1 and the Fig. 1a caption only speak of a 'Design Domain' for a 2-D cantilever beam. No length, height, aspect ratio or even rectangular shape is given in the text; the proportions appear only in Figs. 1a/1d, 2a-c, 3a and A1-A3.

items.entity: finite-element grid (number of design sites N)
items.description: N, 'the number of elements to deposit material in' (App. A), is never given. Sec. II.4 and Figs. A1/A2 (one panel per site) suggest a coarse grid, but nelx x nely and the element type (presumably square bilinear Q4 with one density per element) are not stated.
Supports are called only 'Fixed Nodes' (Fig. 1a caption) and 'fixed sites/nodes' (Secs. II.1, II.3). Which edge, and whether the whole edge or only part of it is restrained, is shown only in Fig. 1a.
readings: all nodes on the left edge x = 0, 0 <= y <= H
only a central segment of the left edge (e.g. H/3 <= y <= 2H/3)
a few discrete nodes on the left edge (e.g. at/near the top and bottom corners)

items.entity: restrained DOFs at the fixed nodes
items.description: 'Fixed Nodes' and 'cantilever' suggest full clamping, but the text never says which displacement components are restrained.
readings: u_x = u_y = 0 at every support node (clamped)
u_x = 0 on all support nodes, u_y = 0 at a single node only (roller-type)

items.entity: applied force on the free end ('load-bearing nodes')
items.description: The text mentions only 'Applied Forces' (Fig. 1a caption) and 'load-bearing nodes/sites' (Secs. II.1, II.3). Where on the free end the load acts is shown only in Fig. 1a.
readings: free edge x = L at y = 0 (bottom corner)
free edge x = L at y = 0.5H (mid-height)
free edge x = L at y = H (top corner)

items.description: 'Applied Forces' and 'load-bearing nodes' are plural (Fig. 1a caption, Sec. II.1). It is not stated whether this is one nodal point force in a single load case, a force spread over several nodes, or an edge traction.
readings: total force split equally over 2-3 adjacent nodes
uniform shear traction over the whole free-end edge

items.description: The force direction is never stated. 'Cantilever beam' implies a transverse load, but its sense and any inclination are drawn only in Fig. 1a. Flipping the sign alone leaves the minimum-compliance layout unchanged; an inclined load would change it.
readings: inclined force with an axial component

items.description: No load magnitude is given anywhere. It scales the compliance and therefore the quoted temperatures ('all temperatures are given in units of compliance', e.g. T ~ 3.3, 17.2, 20.7 in Sec. II.1).
Neither E0 nor the thickness is given; Sec. IV.1 refers only to the 'stiffness equation'. They only scale the compliance and the temperature scale.
readings: physical values, e.g. E0 = 210 GPa, t = 1

items.description: Not stated anywhere in the text.
The text does not say whether the 2-D cantilever is plane stress or plane strain.
The text only says x_e is in [0,1] and that 'a higher density reduces compliance' (Fig. 1a caption). The stiffness-density law and the penalty exponent are never given.
Sites may take x = 0, 'void of material' (Sec. II.1), so the stiffness must be regularized, but no Emin or density lower bound is stated.
App. C and the Fig. A3 caption say a density filter was used and that it interacts with the boundaries, but no radius is given.

items.entity: filter type/weights (MD runs vs. Fig. 3a reference optimum)
items.description: Only App. C mentions 'a density filter', and only for the MD ensembles. The weight function, the boundary treatment, any projection, and which filter produced the 'optimized solution as solved by [17]' (Fig. 3a; the reference is unavailable) are all unstated. 'Filter' in the title means the Laplace transform, not this filter.
readings: linear cone (hat) density filter, no projection

items.entity: quantity on which V_f = 0.5 is imposed
items.description: V_f = 0.5 is stated (Sec. II.1), and Eqs. (3)/(5) and App. A impose it as an equality on the particle positions x_e. With a density filter (App. C), it is unclear whether a standard solver should constrain raw or filtered densities (and equality vs. the usual <=).
readings: sum of raw design variables x_e = 0.5 N (equality)
sum of filtered physical densities <= 0.5 N

items.entity: optimizer for the deterministic reference solution
items.description: Fig. 3a is 'as solved by [17]', but the reference list was removed, so the code's identity is unknown. The update scheme, move limit, initial design, stopping criterion and iteration count are not given.
readings: OC update, move limit 0.2, uniform start x_e = 0.5, stop when max change < 0.01
MMA with the same start and stopping rule

items.description: Sec. IV.1 defines C as the integral of strain-energy density (= 1/2 u^T K u). Standard codes such as [17] use C = F^T u = u^T K u. This factor of 2 changes the reported compliance and the temperature scale only.
readings: C = F^T u = u^T K u
C = 1/2 u^T K u (literal strain-energy integral)

items.description: No passive regions are mentioned. 'Design Domain' (Fig. 1a) and 'each design domain site as a particle' (Sec. II.1) suggest that every element is designable, but this is not stated (e.g. there could be a solid pad under the point load).
readings: none: every element is a design variable
small solid non-design pad around the loaded node(s)

items.description: Figs. 1d and 2a-c show finite-T ensemble means. The thermostat settings are not given: chain length (written inconsistently as N_c, N_x and M in App. A, and a plain 'Nose-Hoover thermostat' in Sec. II.1), Nose masses Q_k, time step, integrator, number of samples and T grid. A deterministic solver can only reproduce the T->0 limit (Sec. III).
readings: deterministic optimum = T->0 limit, compare with Fig. 3a
finite-T ensemble mean (e.g. T ~ 3.3, 5 or 9 in compliance units), which needs the unstated MD settings
